title: Analysis
description: The complete set of Facts produced from one Program on one Python version.

pythonVersion.description: The version of the Python that produced this Analysis, such as 3.14.2.

program.description: The Program as analyzed: the learner's text as a file saved by a code editor, so it ends with a newline.

fileName.description: The name the Program was saved under for the Try it yourself commands, such as program.py.

bytes.description: The Program's bytes in UTF-8, in order: zoom level 2.

encoding.description: The encoding tokenize read the bytes with, from its ENCODING token, such as utf-8. Null if it couldn't tell, because the Program names an encoding Python doesn't know.

tokens.description: The Program's tokens, in order, as tokenize finds them, leaving out its ENCODING token: zoom level 3. A Program that breaks the tokenizer has the tokens found before the break.

ast.description: The Program's syntax tree, as ast finds it: zoom level 4. The nodes come in the order `python -m ast` prints them: a node, then the nodes in each of its fields, in turn, so the first is the Module. Empty if the Program has a syntax error.

bytecode.description: The Program's code objects, each with its steps as dis shows them before anything runs: zoom level 5. The file's own comes first, then each one inside it, depth first, in the order Python stores them, so a CodeIndex finds one. Empty if the Program has a syntax error.

stdout.description: Everything the Program wrote to standard output when it ran.

stderr.description: Everything the Program wrote to standard error when it ran, including the traceback of an error that stopped it.

writes.description: Each piece the Program handed to sys.stdout or sys.stderr, and each flush it asked for, in order. print hands over what it was given, the spaces between, and the newline at the end. The first 2,000 of the Program's own are kept, then Python's own report, if it made one.

error.description: The error that stopped the Program, or null if it ran to the end or called sys.exit.

events.description: Each Event of the run, in order: at most 2,000.

runs.description: Each step run, in the order the steps ran: at most 2,000.

frames.description: Each frame Python made to run one of the Program's code objects, in the order they started: frame-0 is the file's. A step run says which frame it ran in.

objects.description: Each object a plate or a variable pointed to, in the order the replay first saw them. Derived: the replay of the plates names them.

eventsCutShort.description: True if the run had more than 2,000 Events, so events holds only the first 2,000.

runsCutShort.description: True if more than 2,000 steps ran, so runs holds only the first 2,000.

writesCutShort.description: True if the Program handed over more than 2,000 pieces and flushes, so writes holds only the first 2,000 of them.

commands.description: Each Try it yourself command the browser's Python ran on the Program, and what it printed.

OutputWrite.title: OutputWrite
OutputWrite.description: One piece handed to sys.stdout or sys.stderr. Observed.

door.description: Where it goes: 1 for sys.stdout, 2 for sys.stderr, the doors (file descriptors) the operating system gives every program.

text.description: The piece, which can be empty, as print's end="" hands over.

run.description: The step run that wrote it: its place in runs. Left out for a piece written after the step runs were cut short, or by Python's own report.

report.description: True for Python's own report, written after the Program's code stopped: the traceback of an error, colored as Python 3.14 colors it in a terminal, or the message sys.exit was given.

OutputFlush.title: OutputFlush
OutputFlush.description: The Program asking for what waits for sys.stdout or sys.stderr to be sent now, as print(..., flush=True) does. Observed.

door.description: The door it flushes: 1 for sys.stdout, 2 for sys.stderr.

run.description: The step run that asked for it: its place in runs. Left out after the step runs were cut short.

ProgramError.title: ProgramError
ProgramError.description: The error that stopped the Program, as the last line of its traceback names it.

type.description: The kind of error, such as ZeroDivisionError or SyntaxError.

message.description: Python's message, such as division by zero. Empty for an error class the Program defines, whose message could only be had by running its code.

line.description: The line of the Program where it happened, counted from 1, if Python names one.

CodeIndex.title: CodeIndex
CodeIndex.description: Which of the Program's code objects: 0 is the file's own, then each one inside it, depth first, in the order Python stores them.

CodeObject.title: CodeObject
CodeObject.description: One of the Program's code objects, as the compiler made it: the file itself, or one function, class body, lambda or generator expression inside it.

name.description: Its name: <module> for the file, greet for a function, <lambda>, <genexpr>.

qualname.description: Its full name, with the names of the code it sits in: Point.__init__.

line.description: The line it starts on, counted from 1.

names.description: The names its steps look up or store, other than its own variables, in order: co_names.

consts.description: Its fixed values, in order: co_consts.

varnames.description: Its own variables, inputs first: co_varnames.

cellvars.description: Its variables that a function inside it also uses: co_cellvars.

freevars.description: The variables it uses from the code around it: co_freevars.

size.description: How many bytes of bytecode it has, counting the cache entries after some steps.

Const.title: Const
Const.description: One fixed value of a code object: another of the Program's code objects, or a value shown as Python's repr shows it.

value.description: As Python's repr shows it, cut to 80 characters: 'Hello,'.

Step.title: Step
Step.description: One step of a code object, as dis shows it before anything runs.

id.description: Fact ID: bc-0 for the first step of the file's code object, then on through each code object in turn.

offset.description: Where it starts in its code object's bytecode, in bytes.

opname.description: The kind of step, as dis names it: LOAD_NAME.

arg.description: Its argument, a number, or null for a step that takes none.

argrepr.description: What dis says the argument means: print + NULL, to L2. A code object is named without its address: <code object greet>.

bytes.description: Its two bytes: the kind of step, then the argument's lowest byte.

caches.description: How many 2-byte cache entries follow it, where Python keeps notes for rewriting it into a faster form.

line.description: The line it comes from, counted from 1; 0 for a step Python adds before the file's first line; null for a step with no line.

span.description: The code it comes from, if it comes from one place.

jump.description: For a step that can jump, the offset it jumps to.

afterRun.description: The form it had become after the Program ran again, unwatched, as `python FILE`: RESUME_CHECK, LOAD_CONST_MORTAL, or its own opname if it wasn't rewritten. Left out if that run didn't happen.

StepRun.title: StepRun
StepRun.description: One time a step ran, recorded with sys.monitoring INSTRUCTION events. RESUME, which those don't report, is added where each code object starts or carries on after a yield.

id.description: Fact ID: run-0 for the first step run, run-1 for the next, and so on.

offset.description: Which step of that code object ran: its offset in bytes, as dis shows it.

printed.description: What the Program wrote to standard output while this step ran, if anything.

frame.description: The frame it ran in: its place in frames.

caller.description: The frame of the Program's own code that called that frame, which waits under it; null for the file's frame.

plates.description: Derived: how the plates of each frame changed by the end of this step, as the replay works them out with Python's rules. The frames after a step run are those standing when the next step runs: its frame, and the frames waiting under it.

variables.description: Derived: how the variables of each frame changed by the end of this step.

objects.description: Objects seen again at this step whose repr had changed since they were last seen, such as a list something was added to.

platesUnsure.description: True if Python's rules can't account for the plates of this step's frame from here on, so they aren't shown.

Frame.title: Frame
Frame.description: One frame: the workspace Python made to run one of the Program's code objects once, with its own plates and variables.

id.description: Fact ID: frame-0 for the file's frame, then each in the order it started.

Label.title: Label
Label.description: What a plate or a variable holds: a label for an object. madeBy is the step run that made it. object is the object, if the replay can tell which one. An empty plate holds nothing, where a call has no object to go with its function.

PlateChange.title: PlateChange
PlateChange.description: A change to one frame's plates: took plates off the top, then put these on, the last on top.

VariableChange.title: VariableChange
VariableChange.description: A change to one of a frame's variables: it now holds a label, or it was deleted.

ObjectFact.title: ObjectFact
ObjectFact.description: One object a plate or a variable pointed to.

id.description: Fact ID: obj-0 for the first object the replay saw, and so on.

type.description: Its class's name: str, function, Point.

repr.description: As Python's repr shows it when the replay first saw it, cut to 80 characters, for Python's own types: 'Ada', <function greet>. Any other object is named by its class, <Point object>, because showing it would run its code.

size.description: Its size in bytes, as sys.getsizeof gives it, for an object of one of Python's own types. Left out for an object of a class the Program defines, which could run its code to say.

code.description: For one of the Program's code objects, which one.

ObjectSeen.title: ObjectSeen
ObjectSeen.description: An object seen again, whose repr had changed.

Event.title: Event
Event.description: One step recorded while the Program ran, in the Program's own code: a call, a line, a return or an exception.

id.description: Fact ID: ev-0 for the first Event, ev-1 for the next, and so on.

kind.description: Recorded as sys.settrace reports them. call: a code object starts, or carries on after a yield. line: a new line is about to run, or a loop goes back to the start of the same line. return: a code object returns, yields, or ends with an error. exception: an error happens, or passes through.

line.description: The line, counted from 1. For a call, the line the code object starts on, or the line it carries on from after a yield.

locals.description: Each variable of that code object at that moment, by name, as Python's repr shows it, cut to 80 characters. Names that start and end with __ are left out. Only Python's own types are shown that way; any other object is named by its class, such as <Point object>, because showing it would run its code.

value.description: For a return, the value returned or yielded, shown like a variable; none when an error ends the code object. For an exception, the error, such as ZeroDivisionError: division by zero.

CommandRun.title: CommandRun
CommandRun.description: One Try it yourself command, run by the browser's Python on the Program saved as fileName.

command.description: The command, as the learner would type it: python program.py.

output.description: What a terminal shows: everything written to stdout and stderr, in the order it was written.

exitStatus.description: The command's exit status: 0 if it ended normally, 1 after an error, or the number passed to sys.exit.

id.description: Fact ID: byte-0 for the first byte, byte-1 for the next, and so on.

value.description: The byte, a number from 0 to 255.

charIndex.description: Which character of the program this byte encodes, counted in Unicode code points from 0. A character can take up to 4 bytes, which then share a charIndex.

line.description: The line the character is on, counted from 1. A line's newline belongs to that line.

TokenFact.title: TokenFact
TokenFact.description: One token of the Program, as tokenize reports it. A token that takes up no bytes has a span whose start and end are equal.

id.description: Fact ID: tok-0 for the first token, tok-1 for the next, and so on.

type.description: The kind of token, as tokenize names it: NAME, OP, STRING, NEWLINE, INDENT and so on.

exactType.description: For an OP, the exact kind of punctuation, such as LPAR; for any other token, the same as type.

text.description: The token's text. Empty for DEDENT and ENDMARKER.

keyword.description: True for a NAME that Python reserves, such as for or def, as its keyword module lists them. Left out for any other token.

ByteSpan.title: ByteSpan
ByteSpan.description: A run of the Program's bytes, as positions in bytes: from start up to, but not including, end.

AstFact.title: AstFact
AstFact.description: One node of the Program's syntax tree, a box at zoom level 4, as ast reports it. Its span is null if it has no place in the code, as for the Module or arguments.

id.description: Fact ID: ast-0 for the Module, ast-1 for the next node, and so on.

type.description: The kind of node, as ast names it: Module, Call, Name and so on.

parent.description: The Fact ID of the node that holds this one. Null for the Module.

field.description: The field of the parent that holds this node, such as body or func. Null for the Module.

fields.description: The node's fields, in order, as `python -m ast` prints them: it leaves out a field that holds an empty list, or None where None is the default.

AstField.title: AstField
AstField.description: One field of a node: either other nodes, or a value. Markers such as Load, Store or Add are values: they say what the node does, and have no place in the code.

nodes.description: The Fact IDs of the nodes the field holds, in order.

list.description: True if the field holds a list, such as a body, even of one node.

value.description: The value as `python -m ast` writes it: 'print', Load(), 1.

Position.title: Position
Position.description: A place in the Program, as tokenize gives it: the line, counted from 1, and the column, counted in characters from 0. A token's end is the first column after it.

Templates.title: Templates
Templates.description: The Templates for one Python version, in one file, such as templates/py314.json.

pythonVersion.description: The Python version the Templates explain, such as 3.14.

templates.description: Each Template, by its ID, such as byte.newline.

tryIt.description: Each zoom level's Try it yourself command, by level number. A level without one has no Try it yourself section.

ReferenceLibrary.title: ReferenceLibrary
ReferenceLibrary.description: The Reference Library for one exact Python version, such as reference/cpython-3.14.2.json: lines of the interpreter's C source, each with a plain-English sentence, for each handler and how it ran; the machine code of the handlers the Examples ran; and, for the Examples, which handlers ran on each step run and the path each took through its machine code. Zoom levels 6 and 7 show it, labeled Reference.

pythonVersion.description: The exact Python version the C source is from, such as 3.14.2.

entries.description: Each entry, by the handler it quotes and, after a slash, how that handler ran when the C shown depends on it: LOAD_NAME, CALL/python, CALL/c, CALL/rewrites.

functions.description: What each function a handler calls does, in plain English, by its name in the machine code: PyDict_GetItemRef. A function without one is described as another function inside Python.

lineNotes.description: Notes on single machine instructions that ran for one handler run of an Example, ported from prototype v7.

examples.description: The Examples whose handlers were recorded on every step run.

ReferenceSource.title: ReferenceSource
ReferenceSource.description: Where the quoted C comes from: one file of CPython's source at one tag, and the copy the build checks every quoted line against.

repository.description: CPython's repository on GitHub, which the page links to.

file.description: The file in the repository: Python/bytecodes.c.

copy.description: The copy of that file in the repo, from the Reference Library's folder.

sha256.description: The copy's SHA-256, so the build knows it is the file at the tag.

ReferenceEntry.title: ReferenceEntry
ReferenceEntry.description: The C of one handler, as it ran one way: its key lines, each with a plain-English sentence. Its strings are filled in like a Template whose subject is step.

note.description: What is shown, and what is left out.

pathNote.description: What the machine instructions that ran show on a run like this, for zoom level 7.

ReferenceLine.title: ReferenceLine
ReferenceLine.description: One quoted C statement and its sentence. A statement on several lines of the source is quoted on one; the build ignores spaces when it checks it, and a quote ending in … only has to match the start of those lines.

say.description: What the line does, in plain English.

code.description: The C, as it is in the source.

first.description: Its first line in the source, counted from 1.

last.description: Its last line in the source.

ReferenceExample.title: ReferenceExample
ReferenceExample.description: An Example whose handlers were recorded with a debugger on every step run. A Program gets them only if it is this Example and its step runs are these, in this order.

name.description: The Example's name: hello world, greet.py.

program.description: The Program, ending with a newline, as the Analysis has it.

recorded.description: How the handlers were recorded, and on which build of Python.

runs.description: Each step run, in the order the steps ran, as the Analysis records them.

samples.description: The Try it yourself commands a browser can't run, run natively on the test machine for the Example, by zoom level: 7 times it, 8 lists its write system calls with strace.

ReferenceSample.title: ReferenceSample
ReferenceSample.description: A Try it yourself command a browser can't run, run natively on the test machine for an Example: how long it took, or the system calls it made.

command.description: The command, for the Example saved as a file: python -c "… exec(open('greet.py').read()) …".

output.description: What it printed: for timing, the Example's output, then the seconds it took; for strace, its lines, without strace's colors or the Example's own output.

platform.description: The machine and the build of Python it ran on.

ReferenceRun.title: ReferenceRun
ReferenceRun.description: One step run of an Example, and the handlers that ran for it.

offset.description: The step's offset in its code object.

handlers.description: The handlers that ran, in order. A step that rewrote itself runs two: its general form, then the new one.

HandlerRun.title: HandlerRun
HandlerRun.description: One handler that ran for a step run.

inside.description: The handler this one's code ran inside, if the compiler copied it there, so no handler of its own ran: CALL_PY_EXACT_ARGS.

path.description: The address of every machine instruction it ran, in the order they ran, recorded with gdb. Left out if no handler of its own ran.

calls.description: The functions it called, in the order it first called each.

function.description: The function's name in the machine code: PyDict_GetItemRef.

times.description: How many times it called it.

values.description: The number each inc or dec instruction it ran changed, such as a reference count, as gdb read it before and after.

at.description: The instruction's place in the path, counted from 0.

copied.description: Where the path ran another handler's code that the compiler copied onto the end of this one: RESUME_CHECK's, from this place in the path to its end.

LineNotes.title: LineNotes
LineNotes.description: Notes on single machine instructions that ran for one handler run of an Example. Its strings are filled in like a Template whose subject is handler: {before} and {after} are the numbers gdb read where the instruction changed one.

run.description: The step run, as a place in the Example's runs, counted from 0.

handler.description: The handler that ran for it.

note.description: What the instructions that ran show, in place of the entry's pathNote.

lines.description: A note for each instruction, by its address. Each must be on the path.

stages.description: Small headings that split a long handler into stages, by the address of each stage's first note.

MachineCode.title: MachineCode
MachineCode.description: The machine code of each handler the Examples ran, disassembled from one build of CPython by prototype/tools/extract-machine-code.py.

sha256.description: The SHA-256 of its python3.14 program, which the tools check.

MachineHandler.title: MachineHandler
MachineHandler.description: One handler's machine code: its main part, then the .warm and .cold parts BOLT moved elsewhere in the program.

size.description: Its main part's size in bytes.

warm.description: The size of its .warm parts in bytes.

cold.description: The size of its .cold parts in bytes.

MachineInstruction.title: MachineInstruction
MachineInstruction.description: One machine instruction, as Capstone disassembles it.

bytes.description: Its bytes, as numbers from 0 to 255, separated by spaces.

mnemonic.description: What it does, in short: mov, cmp, jne.

operands.description: What it works on, in Intel syntax: rsp, 8.

note.description: Where it jumps or calls: here, within the handler; rare, to its rarely used code; dispatch, to the next step's handler, looked up in the table of handlers; indirect, to an address only known when it runs; or fn:NAME, to a named function or handler.

part.description: The part it is in, if not the main part.

TryIt.title: TryIt
TryIt.description: A zoom level's Try it yourself: a real command the learner can run on their own computer. Its strings are filled in like a Template whose subject is program.

command.description: The command, such as python {file}. The browser's Python runs it on the Program, unless inBrowser is false.

inBrowser.description: False for a command the browser's Python can't run, such as strace. The page then shows what the browser did observe, and a sample from the test machine.

intro.description: What to do before typing the command.

parts.description: The What it does tab: each part of the command, and what it does.

read.description: The How to read it tab: notes on reading the output, after anything the page works out from the Program.

TryItPart.title: TryItPart
TryItPart.description: One part of a Try it yourself command.

code.description: The part, as it appears in the command; … stands for what is inside it.

Template.title: Template
Template.description: Stored explanation text for one kind of element, in one plain-English voice. Filling it in with Facts makes an Explanation. In its strings, {slot} is a Fact value of its subject, **words** are bold, and [[concept|words]] are words with a Concept card.

title.description: The Explanation's heading, if it has one.

term.description: The technical term, shown once in small print, such as code point U+0070.

Subject.title: Subject
Subject.description: What a Template explains, which decides its slots: program, the whole Program (ProgramSlot); byte, one ByteFact (ByteSlot); line, one line of the Program (LineSlot); token, one TokenFact (TokenSlot); node, one AstFact (NodeSlot); step, one Step and, where one is selected, one of its step runs (StepSlot); handler, one handler that ran for a step run, at zoom level 7 (HandlerSlot, and the step run's StepSlot); or output, one line of the Program's output, at zoom level 8 (OutputSlot).

OutputSlot.title: OutputSlot
OutputSlot.description: A Fact about one line of the Program's output, and how it reaches the terminal, that a Template can name. A slot that doesn't apply is empty.

oneOf.description: The line, without its newline or any color codes: Hello, Ada.
Which line it is, counted from 1, in the order they reached the terminal.
The door it goes out through: 1 for standard output, 2 for standard error.
Python's object for that door: sys.stdout or sys.stderr.
How many characters it has, without its newline, with the word: 10 characters.
How many bytes it is in UTF-8, with its newline and any color codes, with the word: 11 bytes.
How many of those bytes are color codes, with the word: 11 bytes.
How many pieces it was handed over in, with the word: 4 pieces.
How many bytes the system call that sent its end writes, with the word: 11 bytes.
How many system calls carried its bytes, with the word: 2 calls.
How many write system calls Python makes for the Program in all, with the word: 2 calls.
How many lines of output there are, with the word: 2 lines.

StepSlot.title: StepSlot
StepSlot.description: A Fact about one step, or one step run of it, that a Template can name. A slot that doesn't apply is empty.

oneOf.description: The kind of step, as dis names it: LOAD_NAME.
Its argument as dis shows it, after a space: the number, then what it means, 0 (greet). Empty for a step that takes none.
Its place in its code object, counted from 1.
Its code object, in words: your program, or the function's name, greet.
The name it looks up or stores: greet, print. For a step that handles two, both: a and b.
The fixed value it gets, as Python writes it: 'Hello,'.
For a call, the code of what it calls, if that is a plain name such as print or name.upper.
How many things a call is given, or a list is made from, with the word: 1 thing, 2 items.
For a sum or a comparison, its operator as you write it: +, <.
For a step that can jump, the step it jumps to: 7.
The form it had become after the Program ran again, unwatched: LOAD_CONST_MORTAL.
How many times it ran, in words: ran once, ran 2 times, never ran.
How many times it ran, as a number: 3.
Which of its runs is selected, counted from 1.
Which step run is selected, counted from 1 over the whole run of the Program.
How many steps ran in all, as a number: 42.
For the selected step run, the object it put on its top plate or stored, as Python's repr shows it, if the replay knows it.
What the selected step run printed, without its last newline.
For a step run of FOR_ITER, which trip round the loop it is, counted from 1.
The step its frame ran next, counted from 1 in its code object.
How many plates all frames hold after the selected step run, with the word: 4 plates.
How many frames there are after the selected step run, with the word: 2 frames.
How many objects the plates and variables point to after the selected step run, with the word: 6 objects.
For the selected step run, the handlers that ran for it, in order, as the Reference Library records them for the Examples: CALL, then CALL_PY_EXACT_ARGS. Empty if it doesn't record them.
For a step run that rewrote its step, the general form that rewrote it: CALL.
For a step run that rewrote its step, the new form it then ran: CALL_PY_EXACT_ARGS.
For a step run whose work ran inside the handler before it, that handler: CALL_PY_EXACT_ARGS.
The Example the Reference Library recorded the handlers of, if the Program is one: greet.py.
For the selected step run, how many machine instructions each handler ran, in words: 33 instructions of CALL, then 107 of CALL_PY_EXACT_ARGS.

HandlerSlot.title: HandlerSlot
HandlerSlot.description: A Fact about one handler that ran for a step run, from the Reference Library, that a Template whose subject is handler can name, besides the step run's own. A slot that doesn't apply is empty.

oneOf.description: The handler: CALL_PY_EXACT_ARGS.
Its name in the program: _TAIL_CALL_CALL_PY_EXACT_ARGS.
How many instructions it has in all parts, with the word: 824 instructions.
How many of them are in its main part, as a number.
Its main part's size, with the word: 3,360 bytes.
The size of its .warm and .cold parts, with the word: 3,166 bytes. Empty if it has none.
How many instructions it ran on this run, with the word: 147 instructions.
Which parts those were in, in words: 5 in its main part, 70 in its .warm part.
The functions it called, in words: builtin_print, _Py_Dealloc 2 times.
The handler whose copied code it ran last: RESUME_CHECK.
How many of the instructions it ran are that code, with the word: 11 instructions.
For a key line, the handler it jumps to or could fall back to: CALL.
For a key line, the function it calls: PyDict_GetItemRef.
What that function does, in plain English.
For a key line, how many key lines in a row say the same, as a number.
For a key line on an inc or dec instruction, the number it changed, before: 3.
For a key line on an inc or dec instruction, the number it changed, after: 2.

NodeSlot.title: NodeSlot
NodeSlot.description: A Fact about one node of the syntax tree that a Template can name. A slot that doesn't apply to the node is empty.

oneOf.description: The kind of node, as ast names it: Call.
The node's own name, without quote marks: print for a Name, greet for a FunctionDef, name for an arg.
A Constant's value as its box shows it: a piece of text without its quote marks, Hello World!, anything else as Python writes it, 42.
The node's code, as it is in the Program: print("Hello World!").
How many statements its body holds, with the word: 1 statement.
How many items a List holds, with the word: 2 items.
For a Call, the code of what it calls: print.
For arguments or an arg, the function it belongs to: greet, or the lambda.
For a For, the code of the name each item gets; for an Assign, what the value is stored in.
For a For, the code of what it goes through: ["Ada", "Grace"].
For an If, the code of its test: x > 1.
For a BinOp, its operator as you write it: +.
For a BinOp, its operator as ast names it: Add.
For an Attribute, the code before the dot: name in name.upper.
How many boxes it holds, at any depth, with the word: 2 boxes. Filled in only where a box is too deep in the tree to draw them.

LineSlot.title: LineSlot
LineSlot.description: A Fact about one line of the Program that a Template can name.

oneOf.description: The line's number, counted from 1.
How many spaces start the line, with the word: 4 spaces.
The line after those spaces, without its newline.

ProgramSlot.title: ProgramSlot
ProgramSlot.description: A Fact about the whole Program that a Template can name.

oneOf.description: How many lines, with the word: 1 line, 5 lines.
How many characters, counting spaces and newlines, with the word: 63 characters.
How many bytes, with the word: 22 bytes.
The name to save the Program under, for the Try it yourself commands: program.py.
How many tokens, with the word: 6 tokens.
The encoding tokenize read the bytes with: utf-8.
How many nodes the syntax tree has, as boxes, with the word: 5 boxes.
The lists of steps the compiler made, in words: one list for your program, and one for greet.
How many steps all the code objects have, with the word: 26 steps.
How many steps ran in all, with the word: 42 step runs.
The Example whose native runs levels 7 and 8's Try it yourself show: the Program itself if it is one, else greet.py.
The machine and the build of Python those ran on.

TokenSlot.title: TokenSlot
TokenSlot.description: A Fact about one token that a Template can name.

oneOf.description: The token's text, as it is in the Program: print.
The kind of token, as tokenize names it: NAME.
The exact kind of punctuation, as tokenize names it: LPAR.
The line it starts on, counted from 1.
The line it ends on, counted from 1.
The column it starts at, counted from 0.
The columns it takes up on its line, in words: columns 0 to 4, column 5, or column 0, taking up no space.
Its place in tokenize's own notation, start line and column, then end line and column: 1,0-1,5.
Its bytes, in order: 112 114 105 110 116.
For an INDENT, what it is made of, with the word: 4 spaces, 1 tab.

ByteSlot.title: ByteSlot
ByteSlot.description: A Fact about one byte, and the character it encodes, that a Template can name.

oneOf.description: Which byte of the Program it is, counted from 1.
How many bytes the Program has, as a number.
The byte, from 0 to 255.
The character it encodes, with a newline drawn as ↵, a space as ␠ and a tab as ⇥.
The line the character is on, counted from 1.
How many spaces indent that line, with the word: 4 spaces.
The character's Unicode number: U+0070.
How many bytes the character takes, with the word: 2 bytes.
All the character's bytes, in order: 195 169.
Which of the character's bytes this is, as a word: first, second, third or fourth.
The byte as 8 bits: 01110000.

ConceptCards.title: ConceptCards
ConceptCards.description: Every Concept card, and the Concepts index that groups them: concepts/cards.json.

cards.description: Each Concept card, by its ID, such as utf8. Text refers to a card as [[utf8|words]].

index.description: The Concepts index: groups of cards, in order. Every card is in exactly one group.

ConceptCard.title: ConceptCard
ConceptCard.description: A short, self-contained explanation of a general computing idea. Its strings can hold **words** in bold and [[card|words]] that open another card.

name.description: The card's heading, such as UTF-8.

related.description: The IDs of related cards, shown as buttons that open them.

ConceptVisual.title: ConceptVisual
ConceptVisual.description: A picture under a card's text.

DoorsVisual.title: DoorsVisual
DoorsVisual.description: The three numbered doors (file descriptors) every program is given when it starts, each with what it leads to. Zoom level 8 shows the same doors.

doors.description: What doors 0, 1 and 2 lead to, in order.

BitsVisual.title: BitsVisual
BitsVisual.description: The 8 bits of one byte, with each bit's value and their sum.

Utf8Visual.title: Utf8Visual
Utf8Visual.description: A table of characters and the UTF-8 bytes that store them. The page works the bytes out; the file only lists the characters.

HonestyLabelsVisual.title: HonestyLabelsVisual
HonestyLabelsVisual.description: Every Honesty label, with what it means. The card that shows it is the one every label chip opens.

ConceptGroup.title: ConceptGroup
ConceptGroup.description: One group in the Concepts index.

name.description: The group's heading, such as Storing text.

HonestyLabels.title: HonestyLabels
HonestyLabels.description: The set of Honesty labels, and which one each zoom level and panel carries: concepts/honesty-labels.json. Changing the set is an edit to this file alone.

labels.description: Each label, by its ID, in the order the How we know card lists them.

levels.description: The label each built zoom level carries, by level number. A level that isn't built yet has none.

panels.description: The label of each panel whose provenance differs from its level.

byteBits.description: Zoom level 2's panel How the number N is stored.

stepRuns.description: Zoom level 5's strip of every step that ran, in order.

plates.description: Zoom level 5's plates of every frame after the selected step run, replayed with Python's rules.

objects.description: Zoom level 5's objects the plates and variables point to.

recipeCard.description: Zoom level 5's recipe card: a code object's names, fixed values and variables.

afterRun.description: Zoom level 5's note on the form a step had become after the Program ran again, unwatched.

noReference.description: Zoom levels 6 and 7 for a step run the Reference Library has nothing for: a hand-written explanation of what the interpreter, or the CPU, does.

registers.description: Zoom level 7's panel on the CPU's registers, worked out by reading the machine code.

outputPieces.description: Zoom level 8's pieces the Program handed to sys.stdout and sys.stderr, recorded as it ran.

reportPieces.description: Zoom level 8's pieces of a traceback, which Python writes after the Program stops, colored as for a terminal.

machineMap.description: The Machine map, beside every zoom level.

terminal.description: The Terminal, beside every zoom level: what the Program printed when it ran.

tryItOutput.description: Try it yourself's What you’ll see tab, when the browser's Python ran the command on the Program.

tryItSample.description: Try it yourself's sample of a command the browser can't run, captured for an Example on the test machine.

HonestyLabel.title: HonestyLabel
HonestyLabel.description: One Honesty label: how the content it is on knows what it shows.

name.description: The word on the chip, such as Observed.

means.description: What the label means, on the How we know card.

warning.description: Shown in the warning color. Only Illustrative is, and the build allows one label at most.
